summary: John's 6th-great-grandmother; wife of Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux and the bridge from the Pennsylvania lines to the Long Island colonial Tuthill/Smith ancestry.
bio: Keturah Tuttle was born in Dec 1755 at Woodbury Clove, Orange Co., NY (SAR application ACN 58344 gives 1755 at 'Woodbury Clove', matching Alva Tuttle). She was probably a daughter of John Tuthill (c.1730-c.1770) and Temperance Smith (Alva Tuttle, Tuttle-Tuthill Lines, 1968, p.311: children twins James & John 1753, twins Ezekiel & William c.1754, Keturah ~1755, Samuel and Daniel); her children's names James, Temperance and Keturah follow that family. Her uncles Capt. Francis Smith and Capt. Austin Smith commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in 1775-76, with her husband as ensign. She married Thomas Lamoreaux and moved with him to Plymouth (1790) and Jackson Twp. His will left her 'my best horse saddle & bridle' and $100. She died 10 Mar 1833 (obituary, Republican Farmer, Wilkes-Barre, 13 Mar 1833; WikiTree Tuthill-530; Find a Grave 269816651, Lamoreaux Family Burying Ground, Jackson Twp). The tree's death of 1842 (tree shows 1755-1842) is her daughter Keturah's (Harvey Book p.360). (Her Tuttle/Smith ancestors are covered in the colonial section.)
sources: Alva M. Tuttle, Tuttle-Tuthill Lines in America (1968) p.311 (FamilySearch Books item 481721: https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/records/item/481721)
